statement: T threads each do K critical sections that increment a plain int, each time passing a fresh queue node from their own stack; the final count is T*K, critical sections never overlap (no data race), and no thread is stuck forever. Run alone first, lock/unlock works and is repeatable.
contract: struct QLock { struct Node; void lock(Node& n); void unlock(Node& n); };  default-constructible and unlocked; Node is default-constructible and must stay alive from lock(n) until unlock(n) returns; the same node is passed to lock and unlock.
scenario_rule: re-acquisition (K >= 2) and three contenders (a queue of length >= 2)
